subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: If the equation ax²+2hxy+by²=0 represents a pair of lines then prove that the equation of the pair of angular bisectors is h(x²−y²)−(a−b)xy=0.

mark_split.label: Split the pair and match coefficients

recall_prompt: Say how you would prove this — say what property defines an angular bisector, and what you substitute at the end.

steps.label: Split the pair and match coefficients
steps.margin_note: First mark. Write the pair as a product of two lines, but in a form that carries the ANGLES the lines make — x sinα − y cosα — because bisectors are about angles.
lines: Let ax² + 2hxy + by² ≡ (x sinα − y cosα)(x sinβ − y cosβ)
On equating like term coeff., we get
a = sinα sinβ,   b = cosα cosβ,   2h = −sin(α + β)  ……(1)

recall.must_convey: That the pair is written as a product of two angle-form lines and a, b, 2h are matched.
accept: write the pair as a product of x sin alpha minus y cos alpha and the same in beta
split the pair and equate the coefficients
a is sin alpha sin beta, b is cos alpha cos beta, two h is minus sin of alpha plus beta
pair ni rendu lines product ga rasi coefficients equate cheyyali
match the coefficients to get the dictionary

steps.why: Every proof in this chapter starts the same way: SPLIT the pair into its two separate lines with unknown coefficients, then match coefficients against the given equation. That dictionary between (a, h, b) and the two lines is what every later step spends.
common_mistakes: Using the slope form m₁x − y, which cannot express an angle bisector cleanly.
Losing the minus sign in 2h = −sin(α + β).

steps.label: Write the bisector equation
steps.margin_note: One mark. A point on an angular bisector is EQUALLY far from both lines, so set the two perpendicular distances equal with a ±. The denominators are each √(sin² + cos²) = 1.
lines: (x sinα − y cosα)/√(sin²α + cos²α) = ±(x sinβ − y cosβ)/√(sin²β + cos²β)
⇒ x sinα − y cosα = ±(x sinβ − y cosβ)      [∵ sin²θ + cos²θ = 1]

recall.must_convey: That the bisector is the locus of points equally distant from both lines, with a ± and unit denominators.
accept: a bisector point is the same distance from both lines so set the distances equal with plus or minus
the denominators are both one because sin squared plus cos squared is one
write the two distances equal
rendu lines nunchi same distance, plus or minus tho
equate the perpendicular distances

steps.why: The two bisectors are perpendicular to each other, and the ± is what produces BOTH of them from one equation — which is why the answer is a pair rather than a single line.
common_mistakes: Dropping the ± and proving only one bisector.
Forgetting that the denominators simplify to 1 and carrying them along.

steps.label: Square and collect
steps.margin_note: One mark. Squaring removes the ±. Use sin2θ for the cross terms so the whole line collapses into differences of squares.
lines: ⇒ (x sinα − y cosα)² = (x sinβ − y cosβ)²
⇒ x²sin²α + y²cos²α − 2xy sinα cosα = x²sin²β + y²cos²β − 2xy sinβ cosβ
⇒ x²sin²α + y²cos²α − xy sin2α = x²sin²β + y²cos²β − xy sin2β
⇒ x²(sin²α − sin²β) + y²(cos²α − cos²β) = xy(sin2α − sin2β)
⇒ x²(sin²α − sin²β) + y²[(1 − sin²α) − (1 − sin²β)] = xy(sin2α − sin2β)
⇒ x²(sin²α − sin²β) − y²(sin²α − sin²β) = xy(sin2α − sin2β)

recall.must_convey: That squaring and using sin2θ collapses the equation to (sin²α − sin²β)(x² − y²) = xy(sin2α − sin2β).
accept: square both sides to remove the plus or minus then collect
use two sin cos equals sin two theta
the cos squared terms convert to sin squared and factor out
square chesi collect cheyyali, sin two alpha vaadali
this gives x squared minus y squared times the bracket

steps.why: Converting cos² to 1 − sin² is what makes the x² and y² coefficients equal and opposite, which is why the answer contains x² − y² rather than two separate terms.
common_mistakes: Forgetting that squaring is what legitimately removes the ±.

steps.label: Substitute back from (1)
steps.margin_note: The last mark. Turn both brackets into product form so that (1) can be used: sin²α − sin²β = sin(α+β)sin(α−β), and sin2α − sin2β = 2cos(α+β)sin(α−β). The common sin(α−β) then cancels.
lines: ⇒ [sin(α + β) sin(α − β)](x² − y²) = 2cos(α + β) sin(α − β) xy
⇒ sin(α + β)(x² − y²) = 2(cosα cosβ − sinα sinβ) xy

lines.text: ∴ h(x² − y²) = (a − b) xy,  that is  h(x² − y²) − (a − b)xy = 0

recall.must_convey: That product formulas let sin(α−β) cancel, and substituting (1) gives h(x² − y²) − (a − b)xy = 0.
accept: use the product formulas so sin alpha minus beta cancels then substitute from one
sin squared minus sin squared is sin sum times sin difference
cos of alpha plus beta is cos cos minus sin sin which is b minus a
product formulas vaadi substitute cheyyali
this gives h into x squared minus y squared equals a minus b x y
heard_as: h into x squared minus y squared

steps.why: cos(α+β) = cosαcosβ − sinαsinβ is exactly b − a from the dictionary in (1), and sin(α+β) is −2h — so the trigonometry converts back into the coefficients the question asked about.
common_mistakes: Cancelling sin(α−β) without noting it appears on both sides.
